_: kogaki#1349: the Move schema's field-to-role mapping. The pipeline reads roles, never field names (specs/spec-draft-pipeline/SPEC.md field-roles table). `required` roles must be mapped by every schema; `optional` roles are null (omitted here) where a schema has nothing to map them to. A field this file does not name is carried on the record and read by nothing. kogaki#1412: `segments` is the Move's structure and is required by the Adapter wherever it is mapped; `technique` is retired and maps no role; `description` is human-facing and maps none. kogaki#1604: `segments` (`operation`, `relation`, `manner`) and `obligation` shape the prose the Move produces; `before`, `after` and `breaks` are read by the Composer for Strand fit and shape no sentence, and no field carries a condition on how a promise is kept. kogaki#1618: `obligation_triggers` is the obligation call's verdict per trigger, written onto a Move record by the library re-judge (`src/proof-sheet/extract.mjs rejudge --library`) and read by nothing in the pipeline; it is named here so a re-judged record still loads. kogaki#1620 (amended 2026-10-29 on the owner's ruling): a Move names no level. The Composer binds any Move from this library to a Leg (/brief) or to a Leg Waypoint (/paragraph-plan); whether an Obligation is kept at Leg or Paragraph level is decided in the Plan, never on the Move, and this schema carries no field for it. kogaki#1698: `takes` and `leaves` are required; the state and obligation roles are optional until their readers move (specs/spec-draft-pipeline/SPEC.md §4.2).

shapes._: kogaki#1414 and kogaki#1413: the shapes of the record's structured fields. A Move record is a `.yaml` file read by the Brief's YAML reader (src/yaml.mjs); the role adapter (`moveContract` in src/compose.mjs) and tools/move_ingest.py both refuse a record that does not hold these shapes. The Moves written before them are regenerated under them by kogaki#1415.
shapes.takes: kogaki#1698: a list, possibly empty, of entries `{ kind, what }` naming what the Move's first Segment takes up on entry, in the terms of what a predecessor could leave; `kind` one of `answer` (a question raised, to be answered), `explain` (a term or item named, to be explained), `carry` (a structure given in a base, to be carried onto the subject) and `apply` (a principle, division or general statement given, to be put to work on a case or shown in an instance), the closed set `MOVE_CONSTRAINT_KINDS` in src/move-validate.mjs; `what` one subject-free line; no two entries alike in both; an entry carries no `segment`; an empty list means the Move can follow any unit; read by judgment, never compared verbatim
shapes.leaves: kogaki#1698: a list, possibly empty, of entries `{ kind, what, segment }` naming what the Move leaves for a later unit of its scale to take up, `kind` and `what` as `takes` gives them and `segment` the number of the Segment that leaves it; an empty list means the Move leaves nothing; a successor need take up one entry and not all, and any later unit may take one up
shapes.state: `before` and `after` are each a map keyed by dimension -- knowledge, question, expectation, orientation, trust -- one entry per changed dimension, each value one sentence; a state written as one joined line is refused by name (kogaki#1413); read by the Composer for Strand fit; shapes no sentence
shapes.after_segment: kogaki#1652: the Segment column of the Extraction's reader table, kept: a map keyed by the dimensions `after` names, each value the Segment number, or comma-separated numbers, after which that `after` state holds, copied from the Extraction's `segment` cell by the ingest; read by no pipeline stage, only by the state-bound re-judge (`src/proof-sheet/extract.mjs rejudge --state`) and checks/check-move-library.sh; a record written before kogaki#1652 carries none and is admitted
shapes.segments: a list of maps, one per Segment, in order: `operation`, the step's operation, subject-free, never its effect on the reader (`does` until kogaki#1510); on every Segment after the first, `relation`, its relation to the Segment before it, in prose; Segment 1 carries no relation (kogaki#1411); and, only where the Extraction filled one, `manner`, the local realisation the step takes that operation and relation cannot name, one line (kogaki#1510)
shapes.breaks: a list of prose tests, one entry each: a specific change to the paragraph, a dash, what the reader loses; read whole, no keys and no fixed kinds; read by the Composer for Strand fit; shapes no sentence
shapes.obligation: absent unless the Move leaves a question standing or a term unexplained, derived from the Move's own Segments and written only where `question` or `term` fires (kogaki#1590, kogaki#1613, kogaki#1618): a question a Segment's operation poses that no later Segment answers, or a term a Segment's operation introduces that no later Segment defines, glosses or grounds; where present a list of one or more items, each a term or a question, one per fired question or term in the order the Segments raise them, naming no item twice (kogaki#1568); an item is one line, or `{item, subitems}` where a later Segment names, without explaining, the parts a question's answer turns on, `subitems` those parts as one-line entries in the order named, closing before their item (kogaki#1620); an item may carry a number or ordinal word, the count forms of kogaki#1602 being retired; it names no level, Leg or Paragraph being the Plan's decision, carries no kind and carries no condition on how an item is kept
